name: 11_chunk_100kb_loses_nothing
why: Chunking used to TRUNCATE a long delta to the last N characters and send only that - the head of a long turn simply disappeared, with no error. Now every piece is persisted (or queued). The fixture is a 161 KB transcript-shaped file that includes one 30 000-character line, so the hard-split path is exercised too. It is pure ASCII on purpose: Go slices bytes and Python slices code points, so only on ASCII can chunk COUNT and BOUNDARIES be compared exactly.
on_failure: rejoin_equals_input false, or a rejoined_sha256 that differs from input_sha256, means that implementation is DROPPING transcript bytes - the exact regression the no-truncation rule was written for; fix before anything else. all_within_limit false means an oversized record will be rejected by the server and queued forever. A chunk_count that changed on only one side is a boundary drift: check core.go splitIntoChunks against hermes-agent/transcript.py split_into_chunks. Verify the fixture itself with: sha256sum fixtures/transcript_100kb.txt
